articles.headline: The Premier League's new villains: Anfield gives Man City a taste of what's to come
articles.description: Man City faced fury at Anfield after being found guilty of cheating, but Erling Haaland and Co. answered the hostility with an emphatic 3-0 win.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグの新たな「悪役」：アンフィールドがマン・シティに突きつけた今後の現実
articles.descriptionJa: 不正行為が認定され、アンフィールドで猛烈な反感にさらされたマン・シティだったが、アーリング・ハーランドらを中心としたチームは、3-0の快勝でその敵意に応えた。
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL -- Manchester City skulked into Anfield on Sunday through the back door, but strutted out of the front at the end of a day when their defiance silenced Liverpool's indignation. They have become the most unpopular team in Premier League history but, for now, they are riding the storm.

Yet as they celebrated a 3-0 victory on the pitch at the end of the game, the City players did so to the tune of "Little Lies" by Fleetwood Mac -- a song played without subtlety by the Anfield DJ.

Enzo Maresca's team may have won the points, but hearts and minds? Forget it.

Having been found guilty by an independent commission during the international break of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules -- City were issued with 115 charges in total -- their trip to Anfield on Sunday was the club's first outing since they were condemned as cheats and accused by Premier League CEO Richard Masters of "systemically breaking rules for almost a decade."

- VAR review: Was Gravenberch wrongly sent off vs. Man City?

- City show defiance in wake of cheating scandal, trounce depleted Liverpool

- Liverpool fans 'welcome' City in first Premier League match since verdict

What a place to show their face again after two weeks of claim and counter-claim since the verdict was announced.

Plenty of teams have reason to feel a sense of injustice because of City's rule-breaking -- the club has appealed the verdict -- but Liverpool arguably suffered more than any other because of the prolonged and industrial scale financial chicanery for which City have been found guilty.

Yes, the period covered by the Premier League investigation was the seasons between 2009-2018, which only saw Liverpool challenge for the title once, when they finished runners-up to City in 2013-14, but the strength and wealth that City accumulated during that time was what made them such a formidable opponent for Jurgen Klopp's great Liverpool team from 2018 onwards.

Had City not inflated their commercial income by over £900 million, as found to be so by the independent commission, Klopp's Liverpool might have at least two more Premier League titles on their roll of honour. In 2018-19, Liverpool amassed 97 points. In 2021-22, they finished the season with 92. On both occasions, City edged them out by a point. Only a team of incredible talent and depth could do that and City, thanks to their ability to outspend their rivals year after year, proved too strong for arguably some of Liverpool's greatest-ever sides.

That's why Anfield was such an unwelcoming venue for City's post-verdict walk of shame. It won't be the only one, though -- Arsenal and Manchester United also have their issues to address with the Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's team.

City knew what was waiting for them, which is why their team bus took an alternative route to Anfield, navigating back streets with a police escort, before entering the stadium through the back door.

articles.body:
Liverpool are looking at Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, while Manchester United are interested in Fulham teenager Josh King.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool see Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis as a potential long-term successor to Alisson Becker, The Sun reports. Tzolakis, 23, has been a standout in the Premier League this season, and Hull are expected to enter talks next month with several suitors keeping tabs on his situation. Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with interest in his signature, with recent reports indicating that his transfer would be valued at £40 million.

- Real Madrid are exploring the transfer market for a midfielder as they also prepare to enter contract talks with Jude Bellingham, according to according to Fabrizio Romano. Madrid are keen to find a midfield anchor after missing out on Rodri following his switch to Barcelona in the summer, but they are first prioritising signing their core players to new deals, with hopes of signing Bellingham, 23, to a two-year extension that will secure his future at the club until the summer of 2031.

- Manchester United are watching the situation of Fulham attacker Josh King after being informed that he could be signed for £50 million, according to Football Insider. The 19-year-old is open to the potential of a switch to Old Trafford, but a deal is expected to be more feasible next summer than in January. Multiple clubs in Europe are also looking at King, who has scored two goals in six Premier League matches so far this season.

- Arsenal are closing in on signing midfielders Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to new contracts, while talks are also ongoing with defender Jurriën Timber, TEAMtalk reports. Arsenal are focusing on securing key players to new deals in the coming weeks after making "significant progress," and they are optimistic of confirming all three extensions before January. Rice, 27, and Odegaard, 27, have both made six Premier League starts this season, while 25-year-old Timber returned from injury last month in the 2-0 league win over Sunderland.

- Liverpool are weighing up their options at right back amid concerns over Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley, with a move for a replacement being considered for the winter transfer window, Football Insider reports. Frimpong, 25, hasn't started a game in the Premier League since August after losing his starting place in the team to Ronald Araújo, while Bradley, 23, is continuing a long return to fitness from a knee injury sustained against Arsenal in January. Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, who has recently been linked with Chelsea, is one of the names on the Reds' shortlist.

articles.headline: QB Tyler Huntley leads Ravens to comeback OT win vs. Falcons
articles.description: With Lamar Jackson still out, Tyler Huntley backed up the Ravens' faith in him by leading them to a 30-23 overtime win against the Falcons, during which Huntley was 11-for-11 passing for 80 yards on the final two drives.
articles.headlineJa: QBタイラー・ハントリーがレイブンズを牽引、ファルコンズに逆転OT勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ラマー・ジャクソンが引き続き欠場する中、タイラー・ハントリーはファルコンズ相手に30-23で延長戦勝利を導き、チームの信頼に応えた。ハントリーは最後の2回のドライブで11回中11回のパスを成功させ、80ヤードを稼いだ。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- On Saturday night, Ravens coach Jesse Minter told his players that there's not a locker room in the NFL that has more confidence in its backup quarterback than Baltimore has in Tyler Huntley.

A day later, Huntley backed up that faith by leading the Ravens to a 30-23 comeback victory over the Atlanta Falcons in overtime.

With starting quarterback Lamar Jackson out because of a sprained left ankle, Huntley delivered the most clutch performance of his seven-year career, going 11-for-11 passing for 80 yards during the final two drives. Looking like the two-time NFL MVP, Huntley tied the score in the final minute of regulation with a 7-yard touchdown pass and then won the game with a 1-yard touchdown on a quarterback sneak.

"[Huntley] is just one of the coolest dudes," Minter said. "He doesn't really get rattled. He just is always the same, and he keeps such a good demeanor about him, keeps his composure. He played with more and more confidence as the game went on and as the moments got bigger, which is really cool to see."

Behind Huntley's performance, the Ravens are 4-1 for the first time in five years and hold a one-game lead atop the AFC North.

Huntley proved once again that Baltimore can prevail without Jackson, as Huntley third straight game as a fill-in starter, but none was as dramatic as Sunday night. With the Ravens trailing 30-23, he tied the score with 40 seconds remaining when he threw a 7-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Devontez Walker, and running back Derrick Henry converted the 2-point conversion.

In overtime, Huntley converted two third downs with passes to Mark Andrews and Zay Flowers before pushing his way across the goal line for the winning touchdown. That 14-play series was the NFL's longest overtime touchdown drive in eight years.

Asked if he relished proving the skeptics wrong -- the Ravens were underdogs for the first time this season -- Huntley said, "Every day is kind of like beating the odds. [There] is not too much [in] listening to them. I am more trying to please my teammates and our organization by getting a win."

The Ravens have repeatedly said they believe in Huntley because of what he has done in the past. He helped Baltimore to two of its biggest wins last season over two playoff teams in the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers.

Leading up to this game, Henry kept telling Huntley that he wanted to see the 2025 Green Bay version of him. In that game, Huntley went 16-of-20 for 107 passing yards and a touchdown in the Ravens' 41-24 victory over the Packers.

"He told me it is 2026, and I won't mention 2025 no more," Henry said.

On Sunday, Huntley didn't look comfortable or decisive in the first half, when he completed 11 of 18 passes (61%) for 97 yards. In the second half, Huntley turned it around by connecting on 13 of his final 14 passes (93%) for 104 yards and two touchdown passes.

articles.description: — With Tyler Huntley filling in at quarterback, the Baltimore Ravens were on Snoop patrol.
articles.headlineJa: ハントリーが終盤にTDドライブで延長戦へ、1ヤードランで得点を挙げレイブンズがファルコンズに30-23で勝利

              When “Snoop” Huntley is leading the offense, the Ravens don't feel like a backup is on the field.


              Huntley led Baltimore to a tying touchdown and 2-point conversion in the last minute of regulation and then scored on a 1-yard sneak in overtime as the Ravens rallied to beat the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 on Sunday night.


              “There's not a locker room in the NFL that has more confidence in their backup quarterback than we have in Snoop,” coach Jesse Minter said.


              Added safety Kyle Hamilton, whose interception in overtime ended the game: “When Snoop gets a chance to go out there, it's a Snoop game. It's not a backup quarterback, and he's done it so any times. It's a blessing to have him.”


              Derrick Henry ran for 102 yards against the Falcons' top-ranked run defense for the Ravens (4-1).


              “If we let it be, this can be a launching point for us to really get this thing rolling,” said Minter after the Ravens took sole possession of first place in the AFC North.


              After Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, Tua Tagovailoa took over at quarterback for the Falcons (2-3) in overtime. Tagovailoa's pass for Drake London was intercepted by Hamilton to end the game.


              “We didn't do enough to win the game,” Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said.


              Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns as the fill-in starter for Lamar Jackson, who has an ankle injury and cheered from the sideline in street clothes.


              Penix overcame a slow start to pass for 240 yards and a touchdown but could only watch from the bench with a towel on his head as the Ravens put the game away.


              Jessie Bates III returned a recovered fumble 36 yards for a score for Atlanta in the first quarter.


              Bijan Robinson ran for 86 yards, but Penix's 5-yard scoring pass to Kyle Pitts was Atlanta's only offensive touchdown.

Huntley targeted Falcons backup cornerback Mike Ford for the touchdown pass a play after Mike Hughes left the game with an injury.

articles.headline: Falcons' Michael Penix Jr. injures rib late in loss to Ravens
articles.description: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. left Sunday night's overtime loss to the Ravens late because of a rib injury, but does not believe it will be a long-term issue.
articles.headlineJa: ファルコンズのマイケル・ペニックスJr.、レイブンズ戦の敗戦終盤に肋骨を負傷
articles.descriptionJa: ファルコンズのQBマイケル・ペニックスJr.は、日曜夜のレイブンズ戦（延長戦の末に敗北）の終盤に肋骨を負傷して退いたが、長期的な問題にはならないと考えている。
articles.body:
ATLANTA -- Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came out of Sunday night's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens late because of a rib injury, but he does not believe it will be a long-term issue.

"Knowing me, I'm going to be ready to go next week because I sat out enough in my career, but I'm going to do everything I can in the training room, make sure I get back to where I want to be," Penix said.

Penix was sacked by linebacker Tavius Robinson with 27 seconds left, with the score tied, and stayed down on the field briefly, but walked off under his own power. Backup Tua Tagovailoa came in for one play and then Penix reentered.

The Falcons ended up having to punt and the game went into overtime, but Penix did not return. Tagovailoa came back in and threw an interception to Kyle Hamilton that ended the game with 2:11 left.

Penix said that if the Falcons got the ball to begin overtime, he probably would have come back in. But as he sat on the bench and got cold during a long Ravens drive to begin the period, the pain worsened.

Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Penix was trying to get comfortable on the bench, but was not able to do so.

"It's frustrating, but I think the biggest thing is just I want to be out there, especially in a big moment in a game like that," Penix said. "I just felt like I needed to be out there."

Penix just returned in Week 3 from left ACL surgery. It was his third ACL surgery; Penix tore his right ACL twice in college.

The Falcons' offense was terrible during the first two weeks of the season with Penix and Tagovailoa (oblique) injured. Third-stringer Cooper Rush led Atlanta to a combined 16 points in Weeks 1 and 2. When Penix returned, the Falcons scored 80 points combined in his first two starts.

On Sunday, Penix was 19-of-32 passing for 240 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions before getting injured.

"I hope he's great," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said of Penix. "I hope that it could maybe only be just a bruise or something like that, and it just felt a little like that in the moment, but I just pray he's all right. I know the whole team does."

articles.headline: NFL Week 5: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 5.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週：日曜日の試合から見る主要なポイント、疑問点、そしてファンタジー的視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationのレポーター陣がすべてのプレーに反応し、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えます。第5週から得られた教訓をお伝えします。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Eagles and Jaguars.

Back in the United States, the first tie of the season came between the Commanders and Giants. The Vikings stayed undefeated despite two fumbles in the red zone against the Saints; while the Texans got into the win column for the first time with a blowout victory over the Titans. The Steelers, led by a big performance from RB Jaylen Warren, dominated against the Colts. And the Packers avenged last season's playoff loss to the Bears.

In the late window Sunday, the 49ers eked out a win over the Seahawks despite losing Deebo Samuel Sr. to injury in the third quarter. The Chargers fell to 0-5 after losing to the Broncos, and the Lions pulled off a comfortable win over the Cardinals.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday's games.

Jump to:

SF-SEA | DET-ARI | DEN-LAC

NYG-WSH | CLE-NYJ | IND-PIT

HOU-TEN | CIN-MIA | LV-NE

CHI-GB | MIN-NO | PHI-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

TB-DAL

San Francisco 32, Seattle 29

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers

Is WR Mike Evans the player who can finally put the 49ers over the top? After failing to score a touchdown in their final two meetings with Seattle last season, the Niners signed Evans to win games like this. Playing through a rib injury for the second consecutive week, Evans finished with seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. He delivered multiple clutch catches to will a sagging San Francisco offense to a huge road victory. Much still needs to fall into place for the 49ers to hoist the Lombardi Trophy again, but Evans has offered a strong answer to one of San Francisco's biggest offseason questions.

What to make of the QB performance: Brock Purdy once again struggled against Seattle's vaunted defense though much of Sunday's game. But as he has many times throughout his career, he delivered when the Niners needed him most. Purdy led two late scoring drives to deliver the winning points, finishing 19-of-29 for 189 yards and two touchdowns with one interception.

Best quote from the locker room: 49ers LB Fred Warner on the team's undefeated start, including road division wins against the Rams and Seahawks: "We're 5-0. We've found a way to win every game and at the end of the day, the goal is to continue to just be on the rise. We're not satisfied with just winning. Of course you want to win every game, but the goal is to continue to get better as the season goes. And I think that sets you up for the best chance to go do what you want to do at the end. I'm really proud of the group. Today was special. It was fun." -- Nick Wagoner

articles.headline: Mike Evans stars in 49ers' win: 'Exactly why he's here'
articles.description: Mike Evans had seven catches, 113 yards and a touchdown to push the unbeaten Niners (5-0, 3-0 NFC West) to a rousing 32-29 victory over the Seahawks.
articles.headlineJa: マイク・エバンスが49ersの勝利で活躍：「これこそが彼がここにいる理由だ」
articles.descriptionJa: マイク・エバンスが7回のキャッチ、113ヤード、1タッチダウンを記録し、無敗を続けるナイナーズ（5勝0敗、NFC西地区3勝0敗）をシーホークスに対し32-29の熱狂的な勝利へと導いた。
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- After 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans introduced himself to the team's rivalry with the Seahawks on Sunday, the superlatives from his teammates and coaches flowed as freely as the coffee that pumps through Seattle.

Linebacker Fred Warner called Evans "a walking aura." Running back Christian McCaffrey said Evans is "everything we want in a receiver." Wideout Brandin Cooks referred to Evans as a "first-ballot Hall of Famer." Center Jake Brendel kept it simple, noting Evans is an "official grown man."

But it was coach Kyle Shanahan who put it most simply after Evans had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown to push the unbeaten Niners (5-0, 3-0 NFC West) to a rousing 32-29 victory.

"That's exactly why he's here," he said.

Indeed, after the Seahawks handled the Niners twice to end last season, including a 41-6 demolition at Lumen Field in the NFC divisional round, the 49ers wandered into the offseason searching for ways to close the gap on the eventual Super Bowl champions.

Part of that came down to finding a wide receiver who can make things happen when nothing else is working. Enter Evans, the 6-foot-5, 231-pound, No. 7 pick in the 2014 NFL draft.

Coming off an injury-plagued 2025, the 33-year-old Evans sought a new challenge in free agency, landing in San Francisco and quickly becoming quarterback Brock Purdy's favorite target.

"He's a game changer," Purdy said. "If you give him the right looks and give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. ... As a quarterback, any time I have an [opportunity] to go to him, it always feels good. He came in the clutch for us there at the end, the beginning of the game, the third-down conversion, the touchdown."

Through three quarters Sunday, the Niners had just 159 yards of offense and were averaging 4.7 yards per play. All of their 21 points had come either from a defensive score or as a direct result of a takeaway that provided a short field.

Trailing 26-21 and needing a long drive, Purdy and Evans, who was playing through a painful rib injury for the second straight week, found their groove. It started with a 15-yarder over the middle. Four plays later, it was a 9-yarder over the middle. On third-and-10 from the Seattle 49, Purdy and Evans connected over the middle again for 23 yards. Even after a costly intentional grounding penalty on Purdy, he lofted one to Evans down the right sideline for a 28-yard gain on second-and-21. That set up a 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooks, with Evans hauling in the catch on the 2-point conversion for a 29-26 lead.

"I'm on the sideline watching him do crazy stuff," Warner said. "I'm like, we have Mike Evans. I can't believe it. And he's unreal. He really doesn't say anything. He just shows up every week and just works and then goes out there on Sunday and just dominates you."

articles.headline: Lakers center Walker Kessler (finger) nears preseason debut
articles.description: Walker Kessler is closing in on making his preseason debut with the Lakers after he was a full participant in practice Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: レイカーズのセンター、ウォーカー・ケスラー（指の負傷）がプレシーズンデビューに近づく
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日の練習に完全参加したウォーカー・ケスラーは、レイカーズでのプレシーズンデビューを目前にしている。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Walker Kessler, the Los Angeles Lakers' biggest offseason acquisition both literally and figuratively, is closing in on making his preseason debut with his new franchise.

Kessler was a full participant in practice Sunday for the first time since the first two days of training camp, when he jammed his left pinkie finger on the backboard while attempting to block a shot.

The 7-foot-2, 245-pound center said he has been limited by the pinkie for "precautionary" reasons. L.A. acquired Kessler in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz in July by sending out two future unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps on top of signing him to a four-year, $130 million contract

"It feels good," Kessler said after showing reporters the black tape wrapped around his injured digit. "Fully went today in practice, felt great."

 

The Lakers have gone 2-1 in the preseason without the big man and have two preseason games remaining: Tuesday against the Golden State Warriors in Las Vegas and Friday at home against the Denver Nuggets.

Kessler, who missed all but five games for the Jazz in 2025-26 after undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder in November, said he is itching to take the court for the Lakers.

"I think it would be a little different if I played last season, but because I didn't play last season, I'm like, 'Ah, I want to play really bad,'" Kessler said. "I'm ready to play, but I trust the staff and I trust the trainers, the coaches and front office, you know? So yeah, just listening to them right now."

Lakers coach JJ Redick was not ready to say if Kessler would play Tuesday against the Warriors.

"A lot can happen in 48 hours," Redick said. "We'll be smart with it. See how he feels [Monday]. But not willing to commit to him playing Tuesday or not. He'll get some live play at some point this week."

The right-handed Kessler spent time after practice shooting free throws and jump hooks around the basket.

While he has been a competent offensive player in his four seasons in the league -- averaging 9.5 points on 68.1% shooting from the field -- he was brought in to bolster a Lakers defense that finished No. 19 in defensive rating last season out of 30 teams.

Kessler said he noticed the Lakers' defensive effort in the time he has been out.

"I mean it's frustrating, but it's also a really positive to see how well they've done defensively without me out there," he said. "Our wing defenders ... Matisse [Thybulle] and Ziaire [Williams] and Q [Quentin Grimes] and even Jake [LaRavia] are just great on-ball defenders. And I mean Luka [Doncic] and AR [Austin Reaves] are great off-ball, very smart players."

Redick said that given the training camp injuries to Kessler, Williams (left foot contusion) and Collin Sexton (right lower leg issue), he still has not finalized his preferred starting lineup for opening night against the Warriors in 10 days.

articles.body:
AS Roma's Emanuele Lulli has caught the eye of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool, while Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are all looking at bringing Atlético Madrid's Giuliano Simeone to the Premier League. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Premier League clubs are tracking a potential move for AS Roma youngster Emanuele Lulli, according to TEAMtalk. The 19-year-old has caught the eye of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool after a recent scouting trip. Featuring as a right-back, Lulli has started in four of Roma's five games this season, marking his first opportunities with the senior team. While there is interest from those Premier League clubs, as well as Paris Saint-Germain, Roma are trying to secure a new long-term deal for the young defender. 

- Atlético Madrid midfielder Giuliano Simeone has emerged as a transfer target for Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and Manchester City, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old caught the attention of Premier League clubs during the summer, with Spurs believed to have explored the possibility of a switch. Atlético are not keen on an exit for the son of coach Diego Simeone, however, meaning any switch to England would not be easy to complete. 

- Chelsea are showing an interest in Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, according to Sport. The France international started only his second LaLiga match of the season on Saturday's against Getafe, scoring his team's final goal in the 3-0 win. Koundé is also attracting interest from other Premier League clubs, with the Blaugrana open to a transfer after considering moving him on in the summer. 

- Several clubs are monitoring the future of Erling Haaland, Football Insider reports, in case the striker is available in the near future. It follows potential uncertainty at Manchester City, after the guilty verdict from all but one of the charges brought against the club by the Premier League, which is now subject to appeal. With that in mind, teams are circling with Arsenal, Barcelona, and Real Madrid monitoring the situation with clear interest in the striker. Haaland has scored 169 goals in 205 appearances for Man City since his move from Borussia Dortmund, making him a dream target for those three clubs and potentially more teams beyond them. 

- Negotiations between Bayer Leverkusen and Christian Kofane over a new contract are stalling. Florian Plettenberg reports. The Bundesliga club are keen to add another two years to the striker's contract, which would take it to 2031, though the 20-year-old is left unhappy with his  role in the squad. Kofane is the second-choice striker to Patrik Schick, despite a breakout first campaign last time out. The Cameroon forward has interest from the Premier League, a destination that he would like to move to at some point in his career. 

Other rumors

- Julián Álvarez remains a target for Arsenal

articles.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns 'disappointed' with Knicks tabling talks
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns responded to the Knicks' statement that they are tabling all extension talks until later in the season, saying he was "disappointed."
articles.headlineJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズ、ニックスによる交渉保留に「失望」
articles.descriptionJa: ニックスが今シーズン後半まで全ての契約延長交渉を保留すると発表したことに対し、カール＝アンソニー・タウンズは「失望している」と語った。
articles.body:
The awkwardness surrounding the New York Knicks and key players continues in the aftermath of the team announcing it would not negotiate contract extensions until later in the season.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who has been the most vocal Knick amid extension talks since the preseason began, issued a response of his own following Sunday's practice.

"It was news to me," he told reporters. "Very disappointed to say the least. Let's state the obvious: It's business, but there is business on the court for us to handle."

Towns is eligible for an extension worth up to $276 million, but he and the Knicks are at a stalemate. Knicks owner James Dolan has said he will not allow the team to go into the second salary cap apron. According to ESPN's Shams Charania, the Knicks' offer to Towns is for $200 million over four years.

 

Towns was a catalyst in the Knicks winning their first NBA title in 53 years last season, making the All-Star team for the sixth time and averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists in the playoffs.

In addition to Towns, swingman Josh Hart is eligible for an extension eligible, though he has a team option for next season. Reserves Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek are also eligible for new deals. One consequence of avoiding the second apron was losing backup center Mitchell Robinson to the Celtics this summer at a salary starting at $15 million. To replace him, the Knicks signed Andre Drummond for the league minimum ($2.4 million).

The Knicks issued a statement Friday saying they were tabling all discussions on extensions.

"As an organization, our entire focus is preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of," the statement read. "As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Towns has a player option for next season worth $61 million. Should he and the team come back to the table during the season, the star would have to decline that option. Towns said he hadn't thought that far ahead.

"Because I never thought we would get to that point," Towns said. "But I think right now what's best for our team is we just focus on the basketball. It's going to be a fun game tomorrow."

He didn't deny being disappointed. Towns has twice made statements surrounding his contract situation in the preseason, perhaps leading to the Knicks issuing their rare public statement late last week.

"We're all humans," Towns said. "My only philosophy since we won, the only thing I've had in my mind, is about how do we win another one. So for me it's the same focus that I came in this season with: How do we keep the trophy in New York past just this one summer?"

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Gravenberch wrongly sent off vs. Man City?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグVAR判定：グレーヴェンベルフはマン・シティ戦で誤って退場処分を受けたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: VARはしばしば論争を巻き起こすが、判定はどのように下されるのか？専属レフェリーのアンディ・デイヴィスがすべてを解説する。
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Was Gravenberch wrongly sent off in Liverpool-Man City?

Liverpool 0-3 Man City (Oct. 11)

Referee: Chris Kavanagh

VAR: Paul Howard

Time: 62 minutes

Incident: Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch sent off for a second yellow card at a key stage in the match

What happened: Having already received a yellow card early in the match, Gravenberch fouled City's Jérémy Doku and received a second yellow card from Kavanagh.

VAR review: Newly introduced into the Premier League this season, second yellow cards can now be reviewed by VAR, but only if they are factually incorrect, and this situation does not fit this category.

Verdict and insight: Most won't like this second yellow card decision, and it will be viewed as "soft." However, Kavanagh was put into a difficult position by Gravenberch's late, clumsy challenge on Doku, which clearly denied the Man City attacker a promising attack as he had clear opportunity to attack Liverpool in a positive area of the pitch. The subsequent yellow card was not a surprise.

These situations are the worst type of situations for referees, because you really want a second-card offense to be undebatable and obvious to everyone. Technical offenses can be questioned and heavily debated, regardless of whether the referee is correct in law.

Gravenberch can feel aggrieved by his first yellow card. From the replays, it looks like the referee misjudged the contact made by the Liverpool midfielder on Elliot Anderson, and on reflection, a free kick alone would have been a better outcome. However, once a player is on a yellow card and challenges an opponent from behind, as Gravenberch did on Doku, the player is running a very high risk of receiving a second yellow if the challenge is a foul and has consequence.

Liverpool will feel hard done by, but the second yellow card was a correct call from the referee.

VAR: Nick Hopton

Time: 86 minutes

Incident: Possible penalty to Man United for a handball

articles.headline: Kings C Maxime Raynaud (knee) to be reevaluated in 2 weeks
articles.description: Kings second-year center Maxime Raynaud will be reevaluated in two weeks with a patellar subluxation in his right knee.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud suffered a patellar subluxation in his right knee during Saturday night's preseason loss to the Golden State Warriors, according to the Kings. He will be reevaluated in two weeks.

Despite anticipation that the young center will miss the start of the regular season, the diagnosis landed as a collective sigh of relief within the organization, considering their worst fears in the moment.

Raynaud was injured while setting a screen for rookie point guard Darius Acuff. The center's right knee gave out as Acuff curled around him, and Raynaud crumpled to the floor and screamed in pain.

Sacramento coach Doug Christie called timeout and walked out to the middle of the floor to check on Raynaud, who had his hands over his face. As teammates came to his side, team trainers called over the EMT with a wheelchair to help Raynaud to the locker room.

A dispirited Raynaud was wheeled to the X-ray room during halftime and then back to the locker room at the start of the third quarter. While there, Kings general manager Scott Perry and team owner Vivek Ranadive visited him. Ranadive gave Raynaud a hug.

He was eventually helped out of the chair onto a pair of crutches, unable to put weight on his right leg. After the game, he received an MRI in San Francisco, which ruled out any serious ligament damage.

Once he's able to return, Raynaud is expected to play a key frontcourt role behind starting center Domantas Sabonis. Raynaud made the All-Rookie second team last season after averaging 12.5 points and 7.5 rebounds in 74 games, proving to be a significant draft find with the 42nd pick.
